character_facts: Aghnar is a newborn or very young infant judged by the man as physically defective or inadequate.
The large man is ruthless and willing to kill his own child for failing his warrior standard.
The white-haired woman is fiercely protective of Aghnar and reveals the cost she paid to bear him.
The relationship between the man and woman is intimate enough that they share a child and a prior conception ordeal.

continuity_links: This page centers on Aghnar's birth or infancy and a parental conflict over whether he should live.
The dialogue implies an established lineage or culture where producing a powerful heir is critically important.
dialogue_meaning: The man rejects the baby as unfit, describing him as unnaturally light and incapable of becoming a warrior.
He believes the child cannot access full strength because he lacks some connection to the earth.
He proposes that they can replace this child with another.
The woman opposes him and insists Aghnar must be spared.
She explains that having another child is impossible because the extraordinary method used to conceive Aghnar made her permanently sterile.
locations: An interior chamber or room with a bed or padded surface where the infant is placed
lore_facts: A warrior ideal exists in which bodily traits and power determine worthiness.
A supposed link to 'the earth' is presented as necessary for full strength or power.
Aghnar was conceived through an extraordinary blood-based fertilization method involving a drop of his father's blood.
That conception method left the mother sterile, making Aghnar their only possible child.
plot_events: A woman holding an infant cries out in alarm as violence erupts.
A large man argues that the child is flawed and will never become a true warrior.
He says the child's weakness is tied to lacking the 'support of the earth' and lacking full power.
A woman tries to stop him with a blade and insists they must not abandon or kill the child.
She says the child, Aghnar, is the only child they will ever have.
She reveals that conceiving the child required fertilizing her ovum with a drop of the man's blood, leaving her sterile forever.
Despite her plea, the man ends the page poised to stab or kill the infant.
